name: draft-release-blog
conclusion: draft-release-blog (Escalate) specifies 4 of 5 categories: 3 autonomy limits, 4 clarification rules, 7 approval gates, 3 validation rules; none for escalation rules. Strongest: approval gates.

autonomy_limits.conclusion: 3 autonomy limits (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly prose: publishing, modifying the release or committing after drafting.

statements.quote: Do not run any publish/upload commands.
Do not modify the GitHub release.
Do not commit anything to the repo.

clarification_rules.conclusion: 4 clarification rules (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose: inventing statistics, quotes or claims; which release the blog covers; personal POV lines and callback URLs.

statements.quote: Do not invent statistics, customer quotes, partner endorsements, or technical claims not grounded in the PRs, issues, code, or docs you have actually read.
Confirm with the user which release the blog is for.
Before drafting, identify 2-4 places in the planned structure where personal POV would belong, then ask the user:
If auto-completion doesn't fire after they authorize, ask for the full callback URL from their browser and pass it to `mcp__obot-wordpress__complete_authentication`.

approval_gates.conclusion: 7 approval gates (6 mandatory, 1 advisory; 5 conditional), mostly prose: posting to Wordpress only on request; publishing live instead of draft; blog shape and plan before writing.

statements.quote: Posting to Wordpress (step 8) is opt-in: only do it when the user explicitly asks.
When posting to Wordpress, the post status MUST be `draft` unless the user explicitly confirms `publish`. Never default to publishing live.
If no release exists yet, ask the user whether to run `draft-release` first, or proceed by surveying commits directly.
Present the recommended shape to the user before drafting and let them override.
Wait for confirmation or adjustments before writing prose.
Skip this step unless the user explicitly asks for it.
`status`: `"draft"`. Never `"publish"` unless the user has explicitly confirmed publishing live.

validation.conclusion: 3 validation rules (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list: em dash, HTML and title checks before posting.

statements.quote: Run `grep -nF $'\xe2\x80\x94' /tmp/release-blog-<VERSION>.md` (or `grep -nF $'—'`) to confirm no em dashes slipped in. The hard constraints forbid them; the markdown editor sometimes auto-substitutes
Confirm the title in the frontmatter matches the title you're sending to `create_post`.
